_comment: Yashigani SANDBOXED-EXTRACTOR seccomp profile (plan §6 B1, Captain). SU SECURITY-REVIEW TARGET. defaultAction SCMP_ACT_ERRNO => every syscall NOT listed is blocked (fail-closed). This jail runs UNTRUSTED document parsers with egress=none, ro-rootfs, all-caps-dropped, non-root. The worker only needs to: read stdin, decompress a zip (CPU+mem), parse XML via lxml/libxml2, write one JSON object to stdout, and exit. It performs NO network I/O (network is also disabled at the runtime layer — this profile is defence-in-depth, NOT the sole egress control). REVIEW NOTES FOR SU are inline in _su_review_* keys below. This is INTENTIONALLY tighter than the gateway profile (yashigani-gateway.json): NO socket/bind/connect/listen/accept (the worker never networks), NO ptrace/process_vm_* (no introspection), NO mount/pivot_root/chroot/unshare/setns (no namespace fiddling), NO bpf/perf_event_open, NO clone3 with new namespaces.
_su_review_scope: Confirm: (1) the allowlist below is the MINIMUM for stdin-read + zipfile-decompress + lxml-parse + stdout-write under CPython 3.14 on amd64/arm64; (2) NO networking syscalls are present (socket/connect/bind/listen/accept/sendto/recvfrom etc. are ABSENT — verify); (3) clone is allowed ONLY for thread creation (CLONE_THREAD), and that the absence of CLONE_NEWNS/NEWUSER/etc. flags is enforced by the absence of unshare/setns rather than a flag-arg filter (Su: decide if a clone arg-filter on flags is warranted vs the pids_limit=64 + no-new-privileges backstop); (4) whether to drop execve/execveat entirely once Tom's parser slice confirms no liblib subprocess is spawned (currently retained so CPython can re-exec on some start paths; flag if removable).
_su_review_clone: clone/clone3 are allowed for CPython thread creation (lxml/zlib release the GIL but the interpreter still spins threads). Namespace creation is blocked by the ABSENCE of unshare/setns and by no-new-privileges + cap_drop ALL at the runtime layer. Su: consider an arg-index filter pinning clone flags to exclude CLONE_NEW* if belt-and-suspenders is wanted.
_su_review_removable_candidates: execve, execveat — retained for CPython startup robustness; candidate for removal after Tom's parsers confirm no subprocess. fork/vfork are NOT listed (the worker is single-process; pids_limit=64 caps any escape).

syscalls._group: file IO on stdin/stdout/tmpfs only (no network fds — see review)
threading + scheduling (CPython threads; NO new namespaces)
process startup (execve retained for CPython re-exec; see _su_review_removable_candidates)
